mission: search specifically for externally defined trading strategies with complete rules, not for another economic hypothesis
registry_hash_algorithm: sha256 of the canonical JSON of the sources array (keys sorted, separators ',' and ':', UTF-8, ensure_ascii=False)

sources.TITLE: freqtrade-strategies — free buy/sell strategies for the Freqtrade bot

sources.CLAIMED_EDGE: each strategy ships minimal_roi, stoploss, buy/sell signals and indicators; the README declares results depend on the user's pairs, timeframe and timerange
sources.CLAIMED_RETURN: UNKNOWN (README presents results as links/images, no numbers in the text)
sources.TRANSACTION_COSTS_INCLUDED: NO (strategy files carry no cost model)
sources.REPRODUCIBILITY: low: code is public and free, but the traded universe and period are user choices
sources.KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: repo states the strategies are starting points, not ready-to-use systems; 'further optimization to the exchange and pairs used will usually result in better outcomes'

sources.TITLE: Strategy001.py — EMA20/50 cross with Heikin-Ashi confirmation (5m)
sources.AUTHOR: Gerald Lonlas (freqtrade-strategies)
sources.CLAIMED_EDGE: enter on qtpylib.crossed_above(ema20, ema50) with heikin-ashi green bar and ha_close > ema20; exit on crossed_above(ema50, ema100) with ha_close < ema20 and red bar; minimal_roi {60:0.01,30:0.03,20:0.04,0:0.05}, stoploss -0.10, order_types entry/exit limit, stoploss market
sources.CLAIMED_RETURN: UNKNOWN (no backtest numbers in the file)
sources.REPRODUCIBILITY: the rule set is complete and fixed; what is missing is a published period, a published result and a fixed universe
sources.KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: the file itself notes results are overridden by the user's config (minimal_roi/stoploss) and that the pairlist is the user's choice

sources.TITLE: NostalgiaForInfinity — Freqtrade strategy (multi-pair, 5m)
sources.AUTHOR: iterativv
sources.MARKET: crypto spot pairs (USDT/USDC preferred by the author)

sources.TIMEFRAME: 5m (the README says the timeframe must not be overridden)
sources.STRATEGY_FAMILY: multi-condition long/short entry ladder with ROI/stoploss exit ladders
sources.CLAIMED_EDGE: the README states the strategy's rules live in code and that backtesting results are in the comments of individual commit pages; no summary metric is published in the README
sources.REPRODUCIBILITY: the rule code is public and versioned, but the pairlist and the number of open trades are user choices and the published results are commit comments rather than a canonical artifact
sources.KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: README: 'use between 6 and 12 open trades, with unlimited stake' (a range, not a fixed size); the repository ships an auto-updater that keeps changing the strategy, so a replication must pin a commit or release tag

sources.TITLE: Q24 Crypto Guide Strategy — Quantiacs crypto contest example (complete code)
sources.SOURCE_TYPE: documented example strategy with full code
sources.AUTHOR: Quantiacs
sources.ASSETS: top 10 crypto by market capitalisation, redefined monthly from coinmarketcap data, stablecoins excluded ('is_liquid' field)
sources.STRATEGY_FAMILY: dual-SMA trend filter with RSI confirmation, equal-weight long-only
sources.CLAIMED_EDGE: signal = 1 where SMA15 > SMA34 and is_liquid, multiplied by (RSI14 < 34 or RSI14 > 68); weights are cleaned/normalised by qnout.clean into long-only crypto daily allocation; no stop, no target, exit is the signal flipping to 0
sources.CLAIMED_RETURN: UNKNOWN (the page shows the backtest call, not the numbers)
sources.PERIOD: in-sample from 2016-01-01; minimum in-sample Sharpe 1.0 required to be valid
sources.FORWARD_EVIDENCE: YES for the contest as a whole (strategies above Sharpe 1 enter daily live paper trading)
sources.REPRODUCIBILITY: high for the rules (the code is published verbatim), medium for the data (platform-bound) and low for the cost model (not stated)
sources.KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: long-only by contest rule; benchmark is the platform's CRYPTO10 cap-weighted index; the example page shows a download error for the index weights, so the benchmark call could not be reproduced while reading

sources.TITLE: Revisiting Trend-following and Mean-reversion Strategies in Bitcoin (Quantpedia, 2024)
sources.SOURCE_TYPE: research-house article with own backtest and an out-of-sample section
sources.AUTHOR: Quantpedia
sources.STRATEGY_FAMILY: breakout (MAX) and mean-reversion (MIN) on rolling lookbacks
sources.CLAIMED_EDGE: MAX: buy BTC when it prints the maximum price of the previous x days; MIN: buy at the x-day minimum; x = 10/20/30/40/50 evaluated, 10 nominated as most effective. In-sample 2015-11-11..2024-08-20 shows both remain effective; the article's own out-of-sample 2022-02-04..2024-08-20 keeps MAX alive and says buying at MIN 'has not performed well'
sources.CLAIMED_RETURN: UNKNOWN (tables/graphs were not captured numerically while reading)
sources.CLAIMED_DRAWDOWN: qualified as lower for MAX than MIN, without numbers
sources.DATA_SOURCE: Gemini daily BTC open prices at 0:00, 2015-10-09..2024-08-20 (public page)
sources.REPRODUCIBILITY: medium: the signal is fully stated, the exit/sizing are not, and the lookback is chosen after a sweep
sources.KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: no holding/exit rule, no position sizing, no fees or slippage; the nominated x=10 is the best of five lookbacks tested, so the parameter choice carries selection risk; the OOS test is run by the same author

sources.TITLE: Exploration of Algorithmic Trading Strategies for the Bitcoin Market (Crone, Brophy, Ward)
sources.SOURCE_TYPE: academic preprint with a real-money-style test and a reproducibility audit
sources.AUTHOR: N. Crone, E. Brophy, T. Ward (Dublin City University)
sources.STRATEGY_FAMILY: machine-learning direction classification with a risk-tolerance trading rule
sources.CLAIMED_EDGE: next-day direction classifiers; a binary long/cash rule and a risk-tolerance variant are traded on unseen Q1-2021 data: an average profit of 86% matching buy-and-hold, +12.5% over buy-and-hold with the confidence-based rule
sources.CLAIMED_RETURN: +86% over three months (Q1-2021) versus buy-and-hold; +12.5% relative with the risk-tolerance rule
sources.PERIOD: training periods up to 2019; unseen test Q1-2021
sources.TRANSACTION_COSTS_INCLUDED: NO (no fee or slippage model is mentioned)
sources.CODE_AVAILABLE: PARTIAL (the reproduced benchmark's code is on GitHub; the paper's own models are not published)
sources.REPRODUCIBILITY: medium-low: the classifier must be retrained and its hyper-parameters are not frozen, so 'the strategy' is a pipeline rather than a fixed rule set
sources.KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: documents that a prior benchmark (Mudassir et al. 2020) trained on its test data and mis-applied PCA — useful as counter-evidence about the literature's quality; no cost model

sources.REPRODUCIBILITY: low: the object under test is the optimiser, and the optimised parameters are the output
sources.KNOWN_LIMITATIONS: parameter search by construction: the result is a search procedure, not a fixed rule set; no out-of-sample protocol was visible in the part read
